title: cdp open Reuses Existing Chrome and Opens URL as New Tab
desc: wkappbot cdp open <url> first checks for an alive Chrome registered to this project (via Window Property GetLaunchedPort, falling back to FindRunningChromePort over the per-project user-data-dir). When found, it skips ChromeLauncher.LaunchAsync entirely and lets ConnectCdp drive Target.createTarget into a NEW TAB on the existing instance. Only when no live registration is found does it fall through to a fresh Chrome launch. Prevents the duplicate-Chrome-on-9222/9223/9224 storm reported 2026-05-05.
steps: WebOpenCommand entry: set ChromeLauncher.DefaultUserDataDirBase=DataDir and ChromeLauncher.ProjectHash=ProjectRoot.Hash8() so registry lookups see the per-project bucket.

Reuse probe (priority order): 1) ChromeLauncher.GetLaunchedPort() reads Window Property WKAPPBOT_CDP_PORT_<hash8> on parent console/desktop HWND. 2) Fallback ChromeLauncher.FindRunningChromePort(userDataDir) does WMI/CDP scan tied to this project's user-data-dir.

Each candidate port verified live via ChromeLauncher.IsPortActiveAsync; dead ports drop out. WMI/CDP fallback re-binds port via RegisterLaunchedPort so subsequent calls take the fast Window-Property path.

Reuse path: skip LaunchAsync. Print 'Reusing Chrome on port N'. Then ConnectCdp(port, navigateUrl=url) calls GetOrCreateSandboxedTabAsync, which uses Target.createTarget when no host-matching tab exists -- new TAB on existing Chrome, not new process.

Launch path: only when both reuse probes return 0 (no live Chrome for this project). Falls through to ChromeLauncher.LaunchAsync(port, url) with SHA256-derived port (range 9300-9995, 4-port block per project CWD).
--new-window opt-out: skips reuse probe, forces new Chrome process. Reserved for isolated-process scenarios.
Port isolation: ports are SHA256-derived from git project root CWD. Each project gets a fixed 4-port block (e.g. 9300-9303). Never hardcode port numbers -- always use cdp open output.

SINGLETON HANDOFF PATTERN (2026-05-18): When web open / cdp open triggers Chrome singleton mode, the new Chrome process exits with code=0 (not a failure -- it handed off the URL to the already-running instance). OLD behavior: treat exit=0 as error ('CDP endpoint not ready'). NEW behavior: exit=0 during launch = detect as singleton handoff -> call FindRunningChromePort() to locate existing Chrome -> attach via CDP to that port -> navigate via Target.createTarget(URL). Result: no SQLite profile contention (no second Chrome launched), seamless reuse of existing session. Fix: ChromeLauncher.LaunchCore.cs, commit 48eb07e08 + web-open fix.

2026-05-18: cookie banner auto-dismiss added to ask flow (commit 62687d6c1). Before prompt injection, JS checks for close/reject buttons on cookie banners and clicks them silently. AI service domains (chatgpt.com, gemini.google.com, claude.ai) never get Accept clicked -- cookie-consent-ai-strategy: no consent cookie = anonymous quota. 500ms settle after dismiss.

requirements.expect: First call launches Chrome; emits OK <grap>. Window Property and userDataDir-keyed CDP registration both populated.

Second call prints '[WEB] Reusing Chrome on port N (will open URL as new tab via CDP)' and '[TAB:GROWTH] sandbox-miss-create before=K after=K+1'. No new Chrome PID, no new CDP port. netstat listing for 922x ports stays identical before and after.
--new-window flag bypasses reuse and launches a fresh Chrome process even when one is registered. Used only when caller explicitly wants isolated processes.

source_refs.note: Pre-launch reuse probe: GetLaunchedPort -> FindRunningChromePort -> IsPortActiveAsync gate
Target.createTarget call site for tab creation in existing Chrome
